_about: What each Cloudflare Radar industry label covers, shown behind the info icon. Cloudflare publishes no definitions; its glossary says only that industries group businesses by their primary activities. Most labels match LinkedIn's industry list word for word, so for those we summarise LinkedIn's definition (source 'linkedin', with LinkedIn's current name where it changed). Labels with no LinkedIn match are our best reading (source 'cloudflare'). Review before relying on any single description.

Accounting: Accounting, audit, bookkeeping and tax firms.
Airlines/Aviation: Airlines and air transport of passengers or cargo.
Architecture & Planning: Architects and planners who design buildings and spaces.
Arts and Crafts: Makers and sellers of craft goods and supplies.
Automotive: Car makers, parts suppliers and automotive services.
Broadcast Media: Radio and TV broadcasters and their online channels.
Broadcasting: Radio and TV broadcasters. Overlaps with Broadcast Media.
Building Materials: Makers and sellers of construction materials.
Business Services: Broad category of services sold to businesses.
Commercial Real Estate: Owners, brokers and managers of office, retail and industrial property.
Computer Hardware: Makers of computers, components and peripherals.
Computer Software: Companies that make and sell software, including SaaS and apps.
Construction: Builders and contractors for buildings and infrastructure.
Consumer Electronics: Makers of phones, TVs, audio and other home electronics.
Consumer Goods: Makers of everyday products sold to households.
Consumer Services: Services sold to individuals, such as repairs and personal or household services.
Consumer products: Broad category of household products. Overlaps with Consumer Goods.
Cryptocurrency: Crypto exchanges, wallets and blockchain projects.
Design: Design studios: graphic, product and interior design.
Ecommerce: Online shops and marketplaces. Overlaps with Retail.
Education: Broad education category. Overlaps with Education Management and Higher Education.
Education Management: Schools, universities and the organisations that run education.
Electrical/Electronic Manufacturing: Makers of electrical and electronic equipment.
Executive Office: Heads of government and their offices.
Finance: Broad finance category. Overlaps with Financial Services.
Financial Services: Firms that make or handle financial transactions: payments, lending, investing, insurance.
Food & Beverages: Food and drink brands and producers.
Gambling & Casinos: Casinos, betting and online gambling sites.
Gaming: Video game companies and gaming platforms. Overlaps with Computer Games.
Government: Broad government category. Overlaps with Government Administration.
Health, Wellness and Fitness: Gyms, fitness, wellness and nutrition businesses.
Holding Companies: Companies that own stakes in other companies.
Hospitality: Hotels, accommodation, restaurants and related services.
IT Services: IT service providers. Overlaps with Information Technology and Services.
Industrial Automation: Makers of industrial control and automation systems.
Information Services: Libraries, archives, databases and web search portals.
Information Technology and Services: IT consultancies and service firms that build, run or support computer systems for clients.
Internet: Web platforms and online services: marketplaces, social networks, streaming, hosting, data and search.
Internet Service Providers, Website Host: Internet access providers and web hosts. Very little agent traffic.
Legal Services: Legal service providers, including notaries and paralegals.
Leisure, Travel & Tourism: Travel agencies, booking sites, tour operators and attractions.
Local Business: Small local businesses without a more specific label.
Market Research: Firms that gather and sell market and public-opinion data.
Marketing and Advertising: Ad agencies, marketing services and advertising businesses.
Mechanical or Industrial Engineering: Engineering firms in mechanical and industrial fields.
Media: Media companies not filed under a narrower media label.
Media & Internet: Broad media and online category. Overlaps with Media and Internet.
Media Production: Studios producing video, audio and multimedia content, usually for others.
Museums and Institutions: Museums, historical sites and cultural institutions.
Music: Record labels, music publishers and artists.
Newspapers: Newspaper publishers, in print or online.
Non-Profit: Nonprofits. Overlaps with Nonprofit Organization Management.
Online Media: Publishers that put audio and video out only on the internet.
Organizations: Associations and membership bodies without a more specific label.
Print & Digital Media: Publishers working across print and online.
Professional Training; Corporate: Corporate training providers. Overlaps with Professional Training & Coaching.
Public Policy: Policy bodies and think tanks working on public policy.
Publishing: Publishers of newspapers, magazines, other periodicals and books.
Real Estate: Agents, brokers, landlords and property managers.
Recreational Facilities and Services: Leisure centres, parks and recreation businesses.
Retail: Shops selling goods to the public, in stores or online.
Security and Investigations: Security guards, alarm services and investigators.
Sporting Goods: Makers and sellers of sports equipment.
Telecommunications: Phone, mobile, cable and internet access providers.
Website Design & Managment: Web design and site management agencies. Spelling is Cloudflare's.
software: Software companies, under a lower-case label kept separate from Computer Software.
